title: sundial-runtime-pocket-notes-kevin
content:
Quick morning pocket notes — scattershot. Use as my single-source scratchpad for the day (pomodoro windows + triage).

Context: woke to noisy p99 spikes on us-west serving pool (~03:00 UTC). Alerts pointed to KV cache thrash + small-window microbatching. I was on call last night; leaving notes for followups and pairing.

Objective for today:
- 3 x 25min focused blocks: repro / small fix / postmortem draft
- Get a reproducible test that shows p99 regression under mem-pressure and tiny batches
- If repro stable, try KV eviction tweak (+increase cold-prefetch threshold) behind feature flag

Immediate triage checklist (what I did / next steps):
- Rechecked on-call notes: INF-4187 flagged cache-evict noise around 02:48 UTC.
- Collected temporary flamegraphs from night shift (attached to Jira).
- Local repro steps I used:
  1) Start local runtime with 2 workers: ./scripts/run_local.sh --workers=2 --kv-size=128MB
  2) Run loadgen (sequence len distribution skewed): python tools/loadgen.py --qps=180 --seq-dist=short-heavy --batch-policy=auto
  3) Observe p99 with logs: tail -n 500 logs/runtime.log | grep P99
- Baseline numbers (local): p50 ~ 12ms, p95 ~ 48ms, p99 ~ 230ms when kv pressure kicks in.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Cold-prefetch threshold too low: small-batch requests repeatedly miss and do synchronous KV fetches -> latency tail.
2) Auto-batch policy falls back to tiny batches under certain seq-dist distributions; overhead of enqueue/drop per-req amplifies p99.
3) NUMA/CUDA scheduling wobble under 2-worker config causing jitter when GC proxies run (observed coincident times in flamegraph).

Quick experiments to run (priority order):
- EXP-A: raise cold-prefetch threshold by factor 2 in local flag: --kv-prefetch-threshold=0.02 -> run loadgen for 30m and record p99 delta
- EXP-B: force batching policy to fixed microbatch size 8: --batch-policy=fixed --batch-size=8 (compare throughput and tail)
- EXP-C: pin cuda visible devices per worker in local run: CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./scripts/run_local.sh --workers=1 to rule out inter-worker interference

Notes from pairing with Maya (10:30):
- She suggests instrumenting KV latency histogram with percentiles per-key-size; I agree. Add telemetry ticket.
- She reproduced p99 drop with a synthetic workload that alternates 50 fast short requests and 1 long streaming request; borderline scenario.

Open todos (short):
- [ ] Add KV per-key-size histogram metric (INF-4201)
- [ ] Add a canary flag for prefetch threshold (config + rollout plan)
- [ ] Re-run end-to-end with real customer prompt set (ask CS for sample)
- [x] Post initial findings to #runtime-triage (done 03:20 UTC)

Commands & quick snippets I keep copying:
- Gather logs last hour: gcloud logs read --project=redwood-prod --limit=1000 --filter='timestamp>=2026-03-11T02:00:00Z AND resource.labels.cluster="us-west-serving"' > /tmp/p99-logs.txt
- Local run (debug): DEBUG=1 TRACE=kv ./scripts/run_local.sh --workers=2 --kv-size=128MB

Repro pitfalls I've seen:
- Repro needs sustained QPS for at least 10 minutes to trigger eviction cycles; short blasts => false negative.
- Running with ASAN/TSAN changes timing; use perf builds.

Draft postmortem outline (skeleton to flesh out):
- Summary of incident (what customers saw, duration, impact)
- Timeline (alerts -> mitigation -> root cause hypotheses -> experiments)
- Root cause (if confirmed) + contributing factors
- Remediation (config change, rollout plan, followups)
- Postmortem owners + deadlines

Personal notes: coffee low, will take 10m walk after first block. If EXP-A reduces p99 by >30% without throughput loss, schedule canary rollout to staging and tag Arjun for review.

End-of-day acceptance criteria:
- Repro is stable enough to compare 3 configs over 1hr each
- KV histogram telemetry in place (or ticket created with details)
- Draft postmortem started with initial timeline

Random brain dump / fringes:
- Consider opportunistic prefetches for short-lived sessions only; full prefetch for long sessions. Might be a small classifier but could reduce wasted KV work.
- Check if prefetch collisions with autoscaler grace period cause bursts of cache warmups (timing overlap)
- Could try a very small token-bucket on kv-fetch path to smooth spikes

If I get blocked: ping Arjun or Maya, escalate to SRE for infra-side telemetry.

-- Kevin

(temporary note: move to confluence when PM-ready; keep this as ephemeral working log)
